title.zh: 中国的地形与地势：三级阶梯

clips.send: Tarim Basin. About 1000 m (3,300 ft). China’s largest basin, between the Tianshan and Kunlun Mountains. The Taklimakan, China’s largest desert, fills its centre. The Tarim River is China’s longest inland river; rich in oil and gas (start of the West–East Gas Pipeline). Tarim equals biggest basin + biggest desert.
clips.text: Tarim Basin。 About 1000 m (3,300 ft)。 China’s largest basin, between the Tianshan and Kunlun Mountains.。 The Taklimakan, China’s largest desert, fills its centre.。 The Tarim River is China’s longest inland river; rich in oil and gas (start of the West–East Gas Pipeline).。 Tarim = biggest basin + biggest desert.

clips.send: Qinling. east–west. The key dividing line between north and south China (Qinling–Huaihe line).
clips.text: Qinling。east–west。The key dividing line between north and south China (Qinling–Huaihe line).

clips.send: Daba. Between the Sichuan Basin and the Hanjiang valley.
clips.text: Daba。。Between the Sichuan Basin and the Hanjiang valley.

clips.send: Dabie. Between Hubei, Henan and Anhui, east of the Qinling.
clips.text: Dabie。。Between Hubei, Henan and Anhui, east of the Qinling.

clips.send: Tibetan (Qinghai–Tibet) Plateau. Average over 4000 m (13,000 ft). The highest plateau in the world: the “Roof of the World”. Snow-capped ranges and glaciers everywhere; “mountains from afar, flat valleys up close”. It forms the first step. Source of the Yangtze and the Yellow River. Four plateaus in one word each: Tibetan HIGH, Inner Mongolian FLAT, Loess BROKEN, Yunnan–Guizhou RUGGED.
clips.text: Tibetan (Qinghai–Tibet) Plateau。 Average over 4000 m (13,000 ft)。 The highest plateau in the world: the “Roof of the World”.。 Snow-capped ranges and glaciers everywhere; “mountains from afar, flat valleys up close”.。 It forms the first step. Source of the Yangtze and the Yellow River.。 Four plateaus in one word each: Tibetan HIGH, Inner Mongolian FLAT, Loess BROKEN, Yunnan–Guizhou RUGGED.

clips.send: Inner Mongolian Plateau. About 1000 m (3,300 ft). China’s second-largest plateau, on the second step. Wide, flat and open: “you can see to the horizon”. Huge grasslands such as Hulunbuir and Xilin Gol. FLAT: “The sky is vast, the land boundless; the wind bends the grass and you see the cattle and sheep.”
clips.text: Inner Mongolian Plateau。 About 1000 m (3,300 ft)。 China’s second-largest plateau, on the second step.。 Wide, flat and open: “you can see to the horizon”.。 Huge grasslands such as Hulunbuir and Xilin Gol.。 FLAT: “The sky is vast, the land boundless; the wind bends the grass and you see the cattle and sheep.”

clips.send: Directions of mountain ranges. Mountains form the “skeleton” of the land. East–west: Tianshan–Yinshan (north row), Kunlun–Qinling (middle row), Nanling (south row). Northeast–southwest: Greater Khingan–Taihang–Wushan–Xuefeng (west row), Changbai–Wuyi (middle row), Taiwan Mountains (east row). Northwest–southeast: Altai, Qilian. North–south: Helan, Hengduan. Arc: Himalaya. Mountain areas (mountains, hills, rugged plateaus) cover about two thirds of China.
clips.text: Directions of mountain ranges。 Mountains form the “skeleton” of the land。 East–west: Tianshan–Yinshan (north row), Kunlun–Qinling (middle row), Nanling (south row).。 Northeast–southwest: Greater Khingan–Taihang–Wushan–Xuefeng (west row), Changbai–Wuyi (middle row), Taiwan Mountains (east row).。 Northwest–southeast: Altai, Qilian. North–south: Helan, Hengduan. Arc: Himalaya.。 Mountain areas (mountains, hills, rugged plateaus) cover about 2/3 of China.

clips.send: Third step. Mostly below 500 m (1,600 ft). Plains: Northeast, North China, Middle–Lower Yangtze. Hills: Liaodong, Shandong, Southeast Hills. East of it, the land continues under the sea as a shallow continental shelf. Step 3 equals 3 plains + 3 hills.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Helan and Hengduan run north–south; Qilian runs northwest–southeast.
clips.text: Common mix-up: Helan and Hengduan run north–south; Qilian runs northwest–southeast.

clips.send: Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau. 1000–2000 m (3,300–6,600 ft). Rugged land with many small flat basins called “bazi” (坝子). Karst (limestone) landforms are widespread, e.g. the Stone Forest. On the second step; its eastern edge is the Xuefeng Mountains. RUGGED: “No three li of flat land.”
clips.text: Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau。 1000–2000 m (3,300–6,600 ft)。 Rugged land with many small flat basins called “bazi” (坝子).。 Karst (limestone) landforms are widespread, e.g. the Stone Forest.。 On the second step; its eastern edge is the Xuefeng Mountains.。 RUGGED: “No three li of flat land.”

clips.send: Second step. 1000–2000 m (3,300–6,600 ft). Plateaus: Inner Mongolian, Loess, Yunnan–Guizhou. Basins: Tarim, Junggar, Sichuan. Boundary with step 3: Greater Khingan – Taihang – Wushan – Xuefeng. Step 2 equals 3 plateaus + 3 basins.
clips.text: Second step。 1000–2000 m (3,300–6,600 ft)。 Plateaus: Inner Mongolian, Loess, Yunnan–Guizhou.。 Basins: Tarim, Junggar, Sichuan.。 Boundary with step 3: Greater Khingan – Taihang – Wushan – Xuefeng.。 Step 2 = 3 plateaus + 3 basins.

clips.send: Middle–Lower Yangtze Plain. Mostly below 50 m (160 ft). Low and flat, with many rivers and lakes and a dense water network. Called the “land of fish and rice” (鱼米之乡). Includes the Lianghu, Poyang Lake and Yangtze Delta plains. Yangtze Plain equals rivers + lakes + fish + rice.
clips.text: Middle–Lower Yangtze Plain。 Mostly below 50 m (160 ft)。 Low and flat, with many rivers and lakes and a dense water network.。 Called the “land of fish and rice” (鱼米之乡).。 Includes the Lianghu, Poyang Lake and Yangtze Delta plains.。 Yangtze Plain = rivers + lakes + fish + rice.

clips.send: Loess Plateau. 1000–2000 m (3,300–6,600 ft). The world’s largest area of loess, thick yellow soil. Cut into countless gullies: “a thousand ravines and ten thousand gullies”. Serious soil erosion feeds mud into the Yellow River. BROKEN: thousands of gullies. Bounded by Taihang (E), Wushaoling (W), the Great Wall (N), Qinling (S).
clips.text: Loess Plateau。 1000–2000 m (3,300–6,600 ft)。 The world’s largest area of loess, thick yellow soil.。 Cut into countless gullies: “a thousand ravines and ten thousand gullies”.。 Serious soil erosion feeds mud into the Yellow River.。 BROKEN: thousands of gullies. Bounded by Taihang (E), Wushaoling (W), the Great Wall (N), Qinling (S).

clips.send: Tianshan. east–west. Crosses central Xinjiang, splitting it into the Tarim Basin (south) and Junggar Basin (north).
clips.text: Tianshan。east–west。Crosses central Xinjiang, splitting it into the Tarim Basin (south) and Junggar Basin (north).

clips.send: North China Plain. Mostly below 50 m (160 ft). Built mainly by silt from the Yellow, Huai and Hai Rivers. Wide and level as far as the eye can see. China’s second-largest plain; a major wheat area. North China Plain equals “flat as a horse can gallop”.
clips.text: North China Plain。 Mostly below 50 m (160 ft)。 Built mainly by silt from the Yellow, Huai and Hai Rivers.。 Wide and level as far as the eye can see.。 China’s second-largest plain; a major wheat area.。 North China Plain = “flat as a horse can gallop”.

clips.send: Altun. Northern edge of the Qaidam Basin.
clips.text: Altun。。Northern edge of the Qaidam Basin.

clips.send: Qaidam Basin. 2600–3000 m (8,500–9,800 ft). The highest basin in China, inside the Tibetan Plateau. Called the “treasure bowl” (聚宝盆): salt, oil and non-ferrous metals. Qarhan Salt Lake is China’s largest salt lake. Qaidam equals HIGHEST basin equals “treasure bowl”.
clips.text: Qaidam Basin。 2600–3000 m (8,500–9,800 ft)。 The highest basin in China, inside the Tibetan Plateau.。 Called the “treasure bowl” (聚宝盆): salt, oil and non-ferrous metals.。 Qarhan Salt Lake is China’s largest salt lake.。 Qaidam = HIGHEST basin = “treasure bowl”.

clips.send: Nanling. east–west. Divides the Yangtze and Pearl River systems.
clips.text: Nanling。east–west。Divides the Yangtze and Pearl River systems.

clips.send: 第二级阶梯。 海拔 1000—2000 米。 高原：内蒙古高原、黄土高原、云贵高原。 盆地：塔里木盆地、准噶尔盆地、四川盆地。 与第三级阶梯的分界：大兴安岭、太行山脉、巫山、雪峰山。 第二级：三高原三盆地。
clips.text: 第二级阶梯。 海拔 1000—2000 米。 高原：内蒙古高原、黄土高原、云贵高原。。 盆地：塔里木盆地、准噶尔盆地、四川盆地。。 与第三级阶梯的分界：大兴安岭—太行山脉—巫山—雪峰山。。 第二级：三高原三盆地。

clips.send: 黄土高原。 海拔 1000—2000 米。 世界上黄土分布面积最广的高原，黄土层深厚。 地表千沟万壑，支离破碎。 水土流失严重，大量泥沙进入黄河。 “碎”：千沟万壑。东到太行山，西到乌鞘岭，北到长城，南到秦岭。

clips.send: 塔里木盆地。 海拔约 1000 米。 我国面积最大的盆地，位于天山与昆仑山之间。 盆地中部是我国最大的沙漠——塔克拉玛干沙漠。 塔里木河是我国最长的内流河；石油、天然气丰富（西气东输的起点）。 塔里木：最大的盆地 + 最大的沙漠。

clips.send: 云贵高原。 海拔 1000—2000 米。 地形崎岖不平，多山间小盆地“坝子”。 喀斯特（岩溶）地貌广布，如云南石林。 位于第二级阶梯，东缘是雪峰山。 “崎”：地无三里平。

clips.send: 四川盆地。 海拔多在 500 米左右。 位于第二级阶梯，四周群山环绕。 盆地内多紫色土，被称为“紫色盆地”（红色盆地）。 西部的成都平原被誉为“天府之国”。 四川盆地：紫色土 + 天府之国。

clips.send: 青藏高原。 平均海拔 4000 米以上。 世界上海拔最高的高原，被称为“世界屋脊”。 雪山连绵，冰川广布，“远看是山，近看成川”。 构成我国地势的第一级阶梯，是长江、黄河的发源地。 四大高原一字诀：青藏“高”、内蒙古“平”、黄土“碎”、云贵“崎”。

clips.send: 长江中下游平原。 海拔大多在 50 米以下。 地势低平，河湖众多，水网密布。 被誉为“鱼米之乡”。 包括两湖平原、鄱阳湖平原、长江三角洲等。 长江中下游平原：河湖多，鱼米乡。

clips.send: 山脉的走向。 山脉构成了地形的“骨架”。 东西走向：北列天山、阴山，中列昆仑山、秦岭，南列南岭。 东北、西南走向：西列大兴安岭、太行山、巫山、雪峰山，中列长白山、武夷山，东列台湾山脉。 西北、东南走向：阿尔泰山、祁连山；南北走向：贺兰山、横断山脉；弧形：喜马拉雅山脉。 山区（山地、丘陵和比较崎岖的高原）约占全国面积的 3分之2。
clips.text: 山脉的走向。 山脉构成了地形的“骨架”。 东西走向：北列天山—阴山，中列昆仑山—秦岭，南列南岭。。 东北—西南走向：西列大兴安岭—太行山—巫山—雪峰山，中列长白山—武夷山，东列台湾山脉。。 西北—东南走向：阿尔泰山、祁连山；南北走向：贺兰山、横断山脉；弧形：喜马拉雅山脉。。 山区（山地、丘陵和比较崎岖的高原）约占全国面积的 2/3。
